extraction.name: FLEURS
extraction.description: FLEURS is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna
extraction.publisher: Meta AI Research, Google Research, Camegie Mellon University
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We start with the FLoRes101 dataset... For each sentence in the 102 languages... we collected three recordings by three different native speakers... After this first recording step, each recording is evaluated by additional workers to assesses whether the recording corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings are discarded
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In the first version of the dataset, about 21.5% of the sentences are missing because none of the three recordings were validated.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: FLoRes-101 contains 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and these sentences have been translated in 101 languages by human translators.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We apply NFC and then FST normalization to each sentence, lower-case, normalize and remove punctuations. We also split words into characters, and define the token jas word boundaries.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: After this first recording step, each recording is evaluated by additional workers to assesses whether the recording corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings are discarded
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: native speakers, imposing a balance in terms of sex ratio of at least 30/70%, when possible.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: We plan to fill these gaps in the future versions of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The goal of FLEURS is to enable speech technology in more languages and catalyze research in low-resource speech understanding.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: FLEURS is well-suited for several downstream tasks including ASR, Speech-to-Text and Speech-to-Speech Translation, Speech LangID, and Multilingual Speech-to-Speech and Speech-to-Text Retrieval.
